topics.topic: Binary configuration read lifecycle and validation timing
questions: After startup, does a binary read use the values captured in `RuntimeSettings`, or reread the current process environment?
Does a missing or malformed BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES prevent startup, or may the service start and refuse only later binary reads?
After startup, do binary reads use the values captured in RuntimeSettings or re-read the current process environment?

quotes: Environment values are read once, by `runtime_settings`, into `RuntimeSettings`; other modules read `config.*` constants or the settings they are handed, never the environment, with two exceptions kept from the running service: `registry_gateway` reads `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` at each Registry call (A6, A30) and `binary_storage` reads `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` and `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` at each binary read, each refusing that call when its value is missing or unusable (Factory code `adapters/registry_gateway.py` `_registry_url`, `adapters/binary_storage.py`; owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated).

`capability:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings` reads and validates the environment variables of A30; a missing, malformed or inconsistent one (a wildcard host or origin, binary bounds out of order) stops the start before any request is served. The Registry endpoint is not one of them: the service starts without it (A6).
judgement.why: The texts distinguish startup validation, which can stop service startup, from binary_storage's explicit exception that rereads both binary variables on every later binary call.

topics.topic: HTTP failure mapping for unusable call-time binary configuration
questions: What declared failure does a call-time missing or unusable binary environment value produce, and is that failure concealed as the document not-found response or exposed as storage unavailable?
What HTTP outcome is produced when an otherwise authorized expense-document read fails specifically because a per-read binary environment value is missing or unusable?

quotes:
`BinaryStorageError` for an unsafe, missing, oversize, unreadable or
unrecognised object.

| `BinaryStorageError` | `binary_storage` | 500 |

  Any other failure is 500. No failure becomes a success, an empty list or a
  zero.
judgement.why: State 5 maps BinaryStorageError and every otherwise unclassified failure to 500; only BinaryAccessRejected raised by expense_management is concealed as 404.

topics.topic: Handling a dynamically changed binary read limit above the startup response ceiling
questions: If BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES changes after startup, who checks the newly read value against the declared response ceiling, and is a value above that ceiling unusable?
If BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES changes after startup to exceed the response ceiling validated at startup, which bound governs the read and what outcome is required?

quotes: The storage read bound is checked to be no larger than the declared response ceiling at start.

Environment values are read once, by `runtime_settings`, into `RuntimeSettings`; other modules read `config.*` constants or the settings they are handed, never the environment, with two exceptions kept from the running service: `registry_gateway` reads `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` at each Registry call (A6, A30) and `binary_storage` reads `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` and `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` at each binary read, each refusing that call when its value is missing or unusable (Factory code `adapters/registry_gateway.py` `_registry_url`, `adapters/binary_storage.py`; owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated).
judgement.why: The texts name no operation or actor that can change the running process environment after startup, so the proposed post-start bound change cannot be made into an admissible witness from the texts.
